static_traits.name: Jonathan Miller
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not yet received psychotherapy; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear logic, concrete expression; fairly cooperative; repeatedly using 'should' phrasing and self-labeling; tone of significant anxiety and self-blame

basic_info.main_problem: I have a persistent thought: I should be more responsible on the road, which makes me feel guilty and anxious while driving. The problem started months ago when I first received a speeding ticket; since then the thought recurs every time I drive, more noticeably when seeing a police car.
basic_info.core_demands: 'It would be a huge relief. I could enjoy driving again and not spend so much energy worrying about things that might not even happen.' (hoping to enjoy driving again, easing anxiety and guilt, no longer spending so much energy on worries that may never happen)
growth_experiences: Received the first speeding ticket months ago, with high stress and feeling irresponsible. Since then the thought 'I should be more responsible' recurs while driving, with stronger anxiety when seeing a police car. Never had similar issues before, nor received counseling; no major physical illness.

special_situations.event: Driving on the road when seeing a police car
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I speed even slightly or am not careful enough, I will definitely be fined again, proving I am an irresponsible person
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Lowering speed, driving more carefully, constantly reminding oneself to follow rules
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will probably get another ticket

special_situations.event: Preparing to drive or just gripping the steering wheel in normal road conditions
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only making zero mistakes counts as responsible; any slight negligence is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessive self-monitoring and tension, striving for zero mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be more responsible; I cannot make any mistakes

special_situations.event: Recalling the scene of being fined for speeding
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One mistake is enough to prove I am essentially an irresponsible driver
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly reflecting and blaming oneself, hoping to remind oneself not to err again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just an irresponsible person

special_situations.event: While driving, thinks of worst-case scenarios that could cause an accident
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If not highly vigilant at all times, the worst will happen (accidents, fines)
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Persistent tension and worry; tries to slow down and avoid any 'risky' movements
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What if something happens or I get pulled over the next second?

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be seen as a responsible and safe driver, and to enjoy driving with peace of mind
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being fined again or causing an accident, being judged as irresponsible, losing self-trust
defense_goal: Avoids making mistakes again or being punished through excessive caution and self-accusation
Maintains vigilance through persistent worry, gaining a sense of safety

object_relations.object_representation: Police/authority are supervisors ready to punish and judge at any time

manifestations: Owning a 'fast car' and enjoying driving freedom, but absolutizing the 'freedom-responsibility' tension after the ticket incident, repeatedly using the self-disciplining statement 'I should be more responsible'
Strongly feeling constrained and judged when seeing a police car, finding it hard to experience the pleasure freedom brings
outcomes: Persistently worrying about the worst-case scenario

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using the statement 'I should be more responsible', internalizing external traffic rules and punishment experiences as harsh self-demands
Treats one ticket as a stable basis for self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessively cautious and tense while driving, repeatedly self-monitoring to avoid any mistake
Devoting much attention to worrying and self-blame, difficult to engage positively with the present driving experience

positive_force: Can proactively adopt more cautious driving strategies and follow rules
Having some social support (having friends and family to talk about average issues with)
Has help-seeking motivation; willing to try new methods to improve the experience
negative_force: Catastrophically anticipating worst-case scenarios (accidents, being fined again)
Introjected 'should' phrasing causing harsh self-criticism and rigid standards
Significant anxiety and guilt while driving, affecting focus and enjoyment

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent anxiety and guilt in driving situations, accompanied by catastrophic worries and 'should' self-criticism
antecedent: Recalling the experience of getting a ticket
Even when following the rules while driving
target_behavior.core_reason: One speeding ticket reinforced black-and-white standards of 'responsibility' and 'should' phrasing, triggering catastrophic anticipation and self-labeling, thus maintaining high anxiety and guilt
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unwelcome outcomes like being fined or accidents through excessive worry and self-restraint (escaping potential danger)
target_behavior.consequence: Declining driving focus and enjoyment, persistent high pressure and exhaustion, every drive plagued by anxiety and guilt
